picks.rationale: A year-and-a-half math problem cracked in five weeks with an AI partner that also slipped in subtle errors — the clearest picture yet of what AI-assisted research actually costs and buys.
picks.excerpt: An AI assistant helped University of Colorado Boulder researchers crack a mathematical problem their lab had wrestled with for a year and a half, in five weeks. It also made subtle errors along the way, exposing both the promise and the limits of AI as a research partner.

picks.rationale: MIT's framework raises the hit rate of computational protein design while pushing models past regurgitating sequences nature already wrote.
picks.excerpt: MIT biologists built a machine-learning framework that raises the hit rate of computational protein design while pushing models away from simply regurgitating sequences that already exist in nature.

picks.rationale: Borrowing clinical-trial blinding for AI benchmarks attacks the field's deepest credibility problem — labs grading their own homework.
picks.excerpt: DeepMind is piloting double-blind evaluation of AI systems, borrowing clinical-trial methodology so benchmark results can't be gamed by labs grading their own homework.

picks.rationale: Nine extra hours of warning is operational, not academic — satellite and grid operators can act on it today.
picks.excerpt: A machine-learning model reading subtle magnetic precursors in solar observations flags coming solar storms up to nine hours before current space-weather methods, buying satellite and grid operators real lead time.

picks.rationale: ML searched solvent formulation space to yield unusually homogeneous quantum-dot films — a materials-processing win that lands directly in display engineering.
picks.excerpt: Machine learning searched solvent formulation space to find recipes that yield unusually homogeneous quantum dot films, a direct materials-processing win for display engineering.
